The checkbox onChange(params, value) hook and slider re-sync from params already exist in renderFields (US-101). The modern (non-legacy) curve, modern_lut / modern_brightness / modern_contrast, is the next story.

userStories.title: Brightness / Contrast modern curve when Use Legacy is off
userStories.description: As an editor, I want Brightness / Contrast with Use Legacy unticked to use PhotoCraft's modern Photoshop-matched curves (modern_brightness then modern_contrast) instead of the legacy math.
acceptanceCriteria: New exported modernContrast(v, contrast) in paint/adjustments.js ports PhotoCraft crates/compose/src/adjust.rs modern_contrast: k = contrast / 128, a symmetric cubic Hermite pivoting at 0.5 with endpoint slope 1 - k and centre slope 1 + k; contrast 0 is the identity and 0, 0.5, 1 are pinned.

New exported modernBrightness(v, brightness) ports the Brightness struct (BRIGHTNESS_KNEE = 126/255, s = 1.375^(|b|/50), e = 1 / (1 + 0.084|b|), Hermite roll-off when alpha² + beta² <= 9 else the power roll-off; lowered brightness inverts the raised curve by 32-step bisection).

New exported applyModernBrightnessContrast(imgData, brightness, contrast, mask = null) builds a 256-entry table of modernContrast(modernBrightness(v, b), max(-50, c)) and applies it to RGB; alpha, fully transparent pixels, and masked-out pixels are untouched.
ADJUSTMENTS.brightness.apply uses applyModernBrightnessContrast when params.legacy is not true and applyLegacyBrightnessContrast when it is true.

tests/paint-brightness-contrast-modern.test.mjs (new) asserts the four reference rows, identity at 0 / 0, monotonicity for brightness -150..150 step 25, alpha and mask handling, and the legacy / modern switch in apply.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.

userStories.title: Hue / Saturation edits one hue range at a time
userStories.description: As an editor, I want Hue / Saturation's Edit menu (Master, Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues, Magentas) so each range has its own Hue, Saturation, and Lightness, weighted by the pixel's original hue, as PhotoCraft does.
acceptanceCriteria: ADJUSTMENTS.hsl gains a dialog-local Edit select ({ local: true }) with options master, reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas. Master shows the existing Hue / Saturation / Lightness rows; each range shows three rows keyed <range>Hue (-180..180), <range>Saturation (-100..100), <range>Lightness (-100..100), default 0, using { group: { key: 'edit', value } }. defaultAdjustmentParams('hsl') gains those 18 keys at 0 and no 'edit' key.

A new exported hueRangeWeight(i, deg) returns PhotoCraft HueRange::neutral(i).weight(deg) for the default bounds [60i - 45, 60i - 15, 60i + 15, 60i + 45] (crates/doc/src/adjust.rs weight): 1 inside ±15° of the centre, a linear fade to 0 at ±45°, wrapping past 0/360. hueRangeWeight(0, 350) is 1, hueRangeWeight(0, 30) is 0.5, hueRangeWeight(1, 120) is 0.

A new exported rangeLightness(rgb01, l) ports adjust.rs range_lightness (move toward the max channel when l > 0, the min when l < 0, by |l|); it matches PhotoCraft's range_lightness_matches_photoshop rows within 2.5.

With Colorize off and any range non-zero, applyHueSatLight adds the summed weighted range shifts (hue degrees, saturation / 100, lightness / 100) to the master values per pixel from the pixel's original hue (adjust.rs HueSaturation arm), clamps saturation to -1..1, applies the master path, then rangeLightness with the summed range lightness. Greys get no range edit. Colorize ignores ranges. All-zero ranges leave the output identical to before.

userStories.title: Levels uses PhotoCraft math with Output Levels
userStories.description: As an editor, I want Levels to map pixels the way PhotoCraft (and Photoshop) do: the midtone gamma is u^(1/g) with the shadow toe above 1, the work is on whole 8-bit levels, and Output black / white set the output range.
acceptanceCriteria: ADJUSTMENTS.levels fields are Input black (0..254, default 0), Gamma (0.01..9.99, step 0.01, default 1), Input white (1..255, default 255), Output black (0..255, default 0), Output white (0..255, default 255), keyed black, gamma, white, outBlack, outWhite. defaultAdjustmentParams(levels) gains outBlack 0 and outWhite 255.

A new exported levelsGamma(u, g) ports PhotoCraft crates/compose/src/adjust.rs levels_gamma: u^(1/g) for g <= 1, and above 1 the toe a·u − b·u^2.2 (a = 2^g) that meets the power curve with the same value and slope. levelsGamma(u, 0.5) is u^2; levelsGamma(0, 2.5) is 0 and levelsGamma(1, 2.5) is within 5e-4 of 1.

applyLevels ports levels_q with quantum 255 (stretch rounded half up to a whole level, gamma rounded, output range rounded) into a 256-entry table. Old saved params without outBlack / outWhite behave as 0 / 255. Alpha, transparent pixels, and masked-out pixels are untouched.

PhotoCraft levels_matches_photoshop rows hold: gamma 2.0 maps 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 224 to within 4 of 4, 30, 55, 90, 128, 181, 221, 239; gamma 0.5 is exact (x/255)^2. levels_work_on_whole_levels holds within 1: input 44..214, gamma 1.78 maps 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 52, 69, 100, 214 to 0, 7, 10, 17, 20, 37, 88, 137, 255.

tests/paint-levels-photocraft.test.mjs (new) asserts the fields, the defaults, the levelsGamma cases, both Photoshop row sets, output range, and mask / alpha handling. Update tests/paint-levels.test.mjs only where it asserted the old pow(t, g) direction.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.

Paint currently raises t to g (inverted direction vs PhotoCraft). Per-channel Levels (Channel select), Auto, and the histogram are later stories.

userStories.title: Levels edits Red, Green, and Blue channels under the RGB master
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a Channel select in Levels so I can set input, gamma, and output levels for Red, Green, or Blue on their own, applied before the RGB master the way PhotoCraft's tone_luts_q chains levels_q(master, levels_q(channel, v)).
acceptanceCriteria: ADJUSTMENTS.levels gains a dialog-local Channel select ({ local: true }) with options RGB, Red, Green, Blue. The existing black, gamma, white, outBlack, outWhite fields are the RGB master and show only while Channel is RGB ({ group }).

Each of red, green, blue gets flat keys <ch>Black, <ch>Gamma, <ch>White, <ch>OutBlack, <ch>OutWhite (same ranges and defaults as the master) that show only while that channel is selected. defaultAdjustmentParams('levels') includes all twenty keys; old params without the per-channel keys behave as identity channels.

applyLevels (or a new exported applyLevelsChannels) builds three 256-entry tables, each lut[v] = master(channel(v)) with the US-105 whole-level levels_q math, and maps R, G, B through their own table. Alpha, transparent pixels, and masked-out pixels are untouched.

A Red-only change leaves G and B bytes unchanged. A channel output range of 0..194 followed by a master input 0..213 matches levels_q(master, levels_q(red, v)) computed directly.

userStories.title: Image menu gains Auto Tone, Auto Contrast, and Auto Color
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Image > Auto Tone / Auto Contrast / Auto Color commands, which read the active layer's histograms (inside the selection when there is one) and apply per-channel Levels with 0.1% clipping.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported autoLevelsParams(imgData, kind, mask = null) in paint/adjustments.js ports PhotoCraft crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs histograms / clip_points / median / auto_adjust: 256-bin R, G, B histograms of opaque-or-partly-opaque pixels (alpha 0 skipped, masked-out pixels skipped), clip 0.001, and returns a levels params object (defaultAdjustmentParams('levels') shape) with an identity RGB master.

kind 'tone' sets each channel's <ch>Black / <ch>White from that channel's clip_points. kind 'contrast' sets all three channels to the clip_points of the summed histogram. kind 'color' does 'tone' and then sets <ch>Gamma = clamp(ln t / ln want, 0.1, 9.99) with t and want each clamped to 0.02..0.98, moving each channel's median onto the mean median. An empty histogram gives identity params.

The Image menu in paint/index.html gains Auto Tone, Auto Contrast, and Auto Color items. Each pushes undo with its label (registered in COMMAND_ICONS in paint/history.js), computes autoLevelsParams on the active pixel layer within the selection mask, and applies them with applyLevelsChannels.

tests/paint-auto-levels.test.mjs (new) ports auto_tone_stretches_a_low_contrast_layer: a 64-wide ramp v = 0.3 + 0.4x/63 with RGB (v, 0.9v, 0.8v) gives, after each kind, pixel 0 below 0.05 and pixel 63 above 0.95 on red (Auto Contrast checks blue at pixel 0 and red at pixel 63). It also asserts the clip_points edge cases (empty → 0..255, the lo < 254 and hi > lo + 1 stops), Auto Contrast's shared points, and mask / alpha handling. A jsdom check asserts the three Image menu items exist.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs histograms, clip_points, median, auto_adjust, test auto_tone_stretches_a_low_contrast_layer. PhotoCraft samples big images on a stride above 4 MP; paint may read every pixel. clip_points returns lo/255 and hi/255; paint's Levels keys are whole levels, so use lo and hi directly. Shortcut Cmd+Shift+L for Auto Tone is optional. The Levels dialog histogram is a later story.

userStories.title: Levels dialog draws the channel histogram and gains the per-channel Auto button
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Levels editor histogram (the selected channel's 256-bin histogram of the layer being adjusted, drawn behind the input sliders) and its Auto button, which sets the selected channel's black / white from 0.1% clipping and resets its gamma.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported levelsDialogAuto(h) in paint/adjustments.js ports PhotoCraft crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_editors.rs auto_levels: clip = floor(total / 1000), lo stops at 253, hi stops at lo + 2, returns [lo, hi] in whole levels. It reuses the clipping walk rather than copying autoClipPoints if the two can share one helper.

A new exported histogramBars(h, width, height) in paint/adjustments.js ports tone.rs histogram_scale_top / draw_histogram: top = max(max bin, 1) * 1.1, and bin i has height min(h[i] / top, 1) * height at x = (i + 0.5) / 256 * width. It returns plain numbers so the drawing is testable without a canvas.

The Levels dialog (paint/adjust-modal.js) shows a <canvas class="levels-histogram"> above the Levels fields with the histogram of the dialog's base image (levelsHistograms with the selection mask) for the Channel select's choice; RGB shows the summed R+G+B histogram (PhotoCraft's luminosity-free composite is a later story). It redraws when the Channel select changes. No other adjustment gets a histogram yet.

An Auto button in the Levels dialog sets the selected channel's Black / White from levelsDialogAuto of that channel's histogram and its Gamma to 1, then previews. On RGB it writes the master black / white / gamma.

tests/paint-levels-histogram.test.mjs (new) asserts the auto_levels stops (empty → [0, 255] guarded, a single full bin, the 253 and lo + 2 stops, a 0.1% tail), histogramBars heights for a known histogram, and a jsdom check that the Levels dialog renders the histogram canvas and the Auto button while Brightness / Contrast does not.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_editors.rs auto_levels and the levels editor (histogram allocated 110 tall above the input sliders), crates/ui-egui/src/tone.rs histogram_scale_top / draw_histogram. levelsHistograms(imgData, mask) from US-107 already builds the 256-bin R, G, B counts. auto_levels differs from edit_cmds.rs clip_points (lo < 253, hi > lo + 2, integer clip); keep both behaviours. userStories.title: Gradient Map edits a multi-stop gradient with PhotoCraft's stop strip
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Gradient Map editor: a gradient strip with stop markers I can click to add and drag to move, a Color and Location editor for the selected stop, Remove and Add Stop buttons, and Reverse / Dither, instead of fixed Start Color and End Color fields.
acceptanceCriteria: ADJUSTMENTS.gradientMap stores its gradient as params.stops, an array of [location 0..1 rounded to 0.001, "#rrggbb"] sorted by location, default [[0, "#000000"], [1, "#ffffff"]]. The startColor / endColor fields are removed. applyGradientMap reads params.stops through the existing gradientMapColor, and a params object with only startColor / endColor (older .paintproj or adjustment layers) still maps as that two-stop gradient. A stops value with fewer than two entries falls back to black → white (PhotoCraft read_stops).

The Gradient Map dialog (paint/adjust-modal.js) shows a <canvas class="gradient-map-strip"> drawing the gradient with one marker per stop; the selected marker uses the accent color. Clicking the strip away from a marker adds a stop at that location in the gradient's sampled color and selects it (at most 64 stops). Pointer down on a marker selects it and dragging moves it, keeping the same stop selected when it crosses another (PhotoCraft move_map_stop).

Under the strip, a Color input and a Location number (0..100 %) edit the selected stop. Remove deletes it and is disabled at two stops. Add Stop inserts a stop halfway along the widest gap in the sampled color there. Reverse and Dither checkboxes stay.

Edits never mutate a params.stops array in place: each edit assigns a new array (see the Curves pattern in paint/curve-editor.js), so Cancel, undo, and adjustment-layer snapshots keep the old stops. Pure stop helpers (sampleStops, moveMapStop, addStopInWidestGap, normalizeStops) are exported for tests.

tests/paint-gradient-map-stops.test.mjs (new) asserts the pure helpers against PhotoCraft's behavior (sample, move-with-rank, widest-gap insert, < 2 stops fallback), that a three-stop gradient maps a mid-gray pixel to the middle stop's color, that legacy startColor / endColor params still apply, and, with jsdom and a 2D context stub, that clicking the strip adds a stop and that Cancel leaves the original params.stops array unchanged.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_editors.rs read_stops / write_stops / sample_stops / move_map_stop / gradient_map_strip / gradient_map (strip 44 tall, bar inset 8 px, marker hit ±6 px below the bar, Add Stop at the widest gap midpoint, Remove disabled at 2 stops, 64-stop cap). The gradient preset picker is a later story. paint/adjustments.js gradientMapColor(stops, t) already interpolates sorted [t, rgb01] stops; reuse it.

userStories.title: Gradient Map gains PhotoCraft's gradient Preset picker

acceptanceCriteria: A new pure module (paint/gradient-presets.js) exports GRADIENT_PRESET_GROUPS ported from PhotoCraft crates/engine/src/presets/gradients.rs builtin(): at least the Basics group (Foreground to Background, Black, White) plus every other group whose stops are plain colors, with GradientPreset::new's even spacing (i / (n - 1)). Stops use 'foreground' / 'background' / '#rrggbb' colors. Transparency stops are dropped (a map has no transparency, as in PhotoCraft gradient_map).
resolvePresetStops(preset, fg, bg) returns a fresh [location, '#rrggbb'] array normalized through normalizeStops in paint/gradient-stops.js.

The Gradient Map dialog shows a 'Preset' <select class="gradient-map-preset"> above the stop strip, with an <optgroup> per group and a leading 'Custom' entry that stays selected after any manual stop edit. Choosing a preset assigns a new params.stops array (never mutating the old one), selects stop 0, redraws the strip, and previews. Foreground / Background come from the paint app's current colors through the dialog deps (fall back to black / white when absent).

tests/paint-gradient-presets.test.mjs (new) asserts the Basics presets' stops, even spacing for a multi-color preset, foreground / background resolution, and, with jsdom and a 2D context stub, that choosing a preset replaces params.stops with a new array and that Cancel on an adjustment layer restores the original array.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_editors.rs gradient_map (Preset combo, selected = 0 on pick) and crates/engine/src/presets/gradients.rs builtin() / GradientPreset::new / resolve. Skip the .GRD import and the user preset library; those need file and preset storage that paint does not have yet.

userStories.title: Gradient tool gains PhotoCraft's Preset option and multi-stop fill
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's options bar to pick a gradient from the same built-in library as the Gradient Map dialog (PhotoCraft's Gradient tool current gradient), so a drag paints a multi-stop gradient instead of only foreground to background.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.gradient gains a { key: 'preset', type: 'select' } option listing 'Foreground to Background' first (the default) and every preset in GRADIENT_PRESET_GROUPS from paint/gradient-presets.js, with option values that name the group and preset. The Gradient tool's onUp resolves the chosen preset with resolvePresetStops(preset, state.color, state.bgColor) and fills through fillLinearGradientStops; Foreground to Background keeps today's result. Undo still goes through pushUndo('Gradient') before the fill.
Transparency stops stay out of scope (presets are opaque, as in US-112); Foreground to Transparent paints the foreground color.

tests/paint-gradient-tool-presets.test.mjs (new) asserts the schema option list, a three-stop preset's pixels at the start, middle, and end of a horizontal drag, the mask skip, the zero-length return, and the two-color equivalence with fillLinearGradient.

userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/engine/src/presets/gradients.rs tool_stops / resolve (the Gradient tool paints the current preset). Radial / angle / reflected / diamond gradient types and transparency stops are later stories.

userStories.title: Gradient tool gains PhotoCraft's Shape option (Linear, Radial, Angle, Reflected, Diamond)
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's options bar to choose PhotoCraft's gradient shape, so a drag can paint a radial, angle, reflected, or diamond gradient with the current preset instead of only a linear one.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.gradient gains a { key: 'shape', type: 'select' } option with values 'linear' (default), 'radial', 'angle', 'reflected', 'diamond', in that order, placed before the Preset option. The Preset option and the hint stay.

A new pure export gradientToolT(shape, x0, y0, x1, y1, x, y) in paint/tools.js ports PhotoCraft algo paint.rs tool_gradient_t: along / len for linear, distance / len for radial, |along| / len for reflected, (|along| + |across|) / len for diamond, atan2(across, along) / 2π wrapped into 0..1 for angle; the result clamps to 0..1.

The Gradient tool's onUp passes toolOpts(state, 'gradient').shape through; undo still goes through pushUndo('Gradient') before the fill.

tests/paint-gradient-tool-shapes.test.mjs (new) asserts the schema option list and default, gradientToolT for each shape at a few points (radial center 0 and edge 1, reflected symmetric about the start, diamond on the axes and the diagonal, angle a quarter turn = 0.25), and a radial drag's pixels at the center and past the radius.

userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/algo/src/paint.rs GradientShape / tool_gradient_t, crates/engine/src/paint_cmds.rs shape names. Transparency stops and Reverse / Dither tool options are later stories.

userStories.title: Gradient tool gains PhotoCraft's Reverse and Dither options
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's options bar to reverse the current gradient and dither it, as PhotoCraft's Gradient tool does, so a drag can paint end-to-start colors and break 8-bit banding without editing the preset.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.gradient gains { key: 'reverse', type: 'checkbox', default: false } and { key: 'dither', type: 'checkbox', default: false }, after the Preset option and before the hint. The Shape and Preset options stay.
A new pure export ditherNoise(x, y) in paint/tools.js ports PhotoCraft color lib.rs dither_noise bit-exactly (u32 wrapping multiplies via Math.imul, >>> shifts, (h & 0xffff) / 65535), returning 0..1.

fillLinearGradientStops takes an options argument (or extra trailing arguments) for reverse and dither: reverse samples the stops at 1 - t; dither adds (ditherNoise(x, y) - 0.5) of one 8-bit step to each RGB channel before rounding, clamped to 0..255 (PhotoCraft algo paint.rs fill_gradient). With both off, pixels match today's output exactly, so tests/paint-gradient.test.mjs, tests/paint-gradient-tool-presets.test.mjs, and tests/paint-gradient-tool-shapes.test.mjs pass unchanged.
The Gradient tool's onUp passes toolOpts(state, 'gradient').reverse and .dither through; undo still goes through pushUndo('Gradient') before the fill.

tests/paint-gradient-tool-reverse-dither.test.mjs (new) asserts the schema keys, order, and defaults; ditherNoise at a few fixed (x, y) values computed from the Rust formula; a reversed horizontal drag paints the end color at the start; a dithered fill differs from the undithered one by at most 1 per channel and is deterministic across two runs.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/algo/src/paint.rs fill_gradient (reverse → 1 - t, dither → (dither_noise(x, y) - 0.5) / 255 on RGB), crates/color/src/lib.rs dither_noise. Transparency stops remain a later story.

userStories.title: Gradient tool gains PhotoCraft's Opacity option
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's options bar to set an Opacity, as PhotoCraft's Gradient tool does, so a drag can lay a partly transparent gradient over the existing pixels instead of always replacing them.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.gradient gains { key: 'opacity', type: 'range', label: 'Opacity', min: 1, max: 100, step: 1, default: 100 } after Dither and before the hint. Shape, Preset, Reverse, and Dither stay.

fillLinearGradientStops' options argument takes opacity (0..1, default 1). At 1 the output matches today's opaque write exactly, so every existing tests/paint-gradient*.test.mjs passes unchanged. Below 1 each pixel is composited source-over onto the existing pixel with source alpha = opacity × the selection coverage (PhotoCraft algo paint.rs fill_gradient → composite_area, Normal blend), with straight-alpha results rounded to bytes.
The Gradient tool's onUp passes toolOpts(state, 'gradient').opacity / 100 through (default 100); undo still goes through pushUndo('Gradient') before the fill.

tests/paint-gradient-tool-opacity.test.mjs (new) asserts the schema key, order, range, and default; a 50% black-to-black fill over opaque white gives mid gray with alpha 255; a 50% fill over a fully transparent pixel gives the gradient color at alpha 128 (±1); opacity 1 matches the opaque fill byte for byte.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/algo/src/paint.rs fill_gradient (opacity multiplies the coverage passed to composite_area). Blend Mode and transparency stops remain later stories.

userStories.title: Gradient tool gains PhotoCraft's Mode (blend mode) option
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's options bar to pick a blend Mode, as PhotoCraft's Gradient tool does, so a drag can multiply, screen, or color a gradient into the existing pixels instead of only laying it on Normal.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.gradient gains { key: 'mode', type: 'select', label: 'Mode', options: one entry per BLEND_MODES value and label from paint/layers.js (or an equal list defined without importing the DOM-touching module), default: 'source-over' } after Dither and before Opacity. Shape, Preset, Reverse, Dither, and Opacity stay.

fillLinearGradientStops' options argument takes mode (default 'source-over'). With 'source-over' the output is byte-identical to today's, so every existing tests/paint-gradient*.test.mjs passes unchanged. Other modes composite with PhotoCraft color blend.rs composite: premul = (1 − as)·ab·Cb + (1 − ab)·as·Cs + as·ab·B(Cb, Cs), ao = as + ab·(1 − as), as = opacity × selection coverage. Separable modes (multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, color-dodge, color-burn, hard-light, soft-light, difference, exclusion) follow PhotoCraft blend_rgb; hue / saturation / color / luminosity reuse blendNonSeparable from paint/retouch.js.
The Gradient tool's onUp passes toolOpts(state, 'gradient').mode through; undo still goes through pushUndo('Gradient') before the fill.

tests/paint-gradient-tool-mode.test.mjs (new) asserts the schema key, order, options, and default; multiply of a #808080 fill over opaque #ffffff gives #808080 and over #000000 gives #000000; screen of #808080 over #808080 gives about #c0c0c0 (±1); a mode over a fully transparent pixel gives the plain gradient color (B is ignored where ab = 0); 'source-over' matches the fill without a mode byte for byte.
Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: PhotoCraft: crates/color/src/blend.rs composite / blend_rgb; crates/algo/src/paint.rs fill_gradient passes the tool's blend mode to composite_area. Transparency stops remain a later story.

userStories.title: Gradient tool honors PhotoCraft preset transparency (Foreground to Transparent, Rainbow Fade)
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the Gradient tool's Foreground to Transparent and Rainbow Fade presets to fade out as PhotoCraft's do, so a drag can lay a color over the image and let the backdrop show through, instead of painting an opaque ramp.

fillLinearGradientStops' options take alphaStops (default null = opaque). With alphaStops null or all 1 the output is byte-identical to today's, so every tests/paint-gradient*.test.mjs passes unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: TOOLS.crop (label 'Crop', icon 'crop', already in ICONS) exists after the marquee and lasso tools; it joins the tool-switch lists in paint/paint.js like the other multi-gesture tools, and setActiveTool / Escape cancel a pending frame.

Pure functions in a new paint/crop-frame.js: cropHit(frame, x, y, handlePx) → 'inside' | one of n / s / e / w / ne / nw / se / sw | 'outside'; cropDrag(frame, hit, dx, dy, opts) moves the frame inside, resizes on an edge or corner (Shift keeps aspect, Alt resizes about the centre), and keeps a 1 px minimum; cropDraw(x0, y0, x1, y1, opts) draws a new frame (Shift square, Alt from centre).

A drag with no frame (or outside it) draws a new frame; the overlay shades outside the frame and draws its handles. Enter (or a double-click inside) commits through the existing canvas-crop path in paint/paint.js with pushUndo('Crop') once, cropping every layer and layer mask; a frame partly past the canvas clamps to it.
TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.crop has a hint plus an 'iconAction' Commit (check) and Cancel (x) pair; both are no-ops without a pending frame.

tests/paint-crop-tool.test.mjs covers cropHit regions, cropDrag move / edge / corner / Shift / Alt / minimum size, cropDraw Shift / Alt, and clamping, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.

acceptanceCriteria: paint/crop-frame.js gains pure cropTurnedAngle(cx, cy, grab, from, x, y, snap) (Shift snaps to 15°), cropNormalizedAngle(deg) (−180..180), cropHitTurned(frame, deg, x, y, handlePx) (hit in the frame's own axes), cropResizedTurned(frame, deg, hit, dx, dy, opts) (handle moves along the frame's axes; the opposite handle stays put on screen), and cropCorners(frame, deg).

userStories.title: Crop Straighten: an options-bar level button arms one line; the frame turns so the line is level (or plumb) and fits inside the image
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Crop Straighten (crates/ui-egui/src/crop_straighten.rs frame_angle, fitted, toggle, pointer, draw) so I can draw along a horizon and have the crop frame turn to level it.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/crop-frame.js: pure cropStraightenAngle(a, b, minLen) ported from crop_straighten.rs frame_angle (with engine analysis_cmds::straighten_angle): the frame angle in degrees (clockwise, normalized like cropNormalizedAngle) that makes the line a→b horizontal, or vertical when it is nearer vertical; null for a line shorter than minLen or a non-finite one.

paint/crop-frame.js: pure cropStraightenFitted(w, h, cw, ch, deg) ported from crop_straighten.rs fitted: the largest frame of w x h proportions turned deg that stays inside a cw x ch canvas, centred on it; null when any size is not a positive finite number.

The Crop options bar gains a Straighten iconAction (Lucide 'ruler' or the icon crop_straighten.rs options_button uses, copied into paint/icons.js if missing) that arms state.cropStraighten for one line; clicking it again disarms it. While armed, a drag through TOOLS.crop draws a line on the overlay instead of editing the frame; on release a line of at least 3 screen px sets state.cropAngle and state.cropFrame from those two functions and disarms; a shorter line only disarms. The edit is a pending frame change: Enter commits and Escape cancels as any crop.

tests/paint-crop-straighten.test.mjs covers cropStraightenAngle (level, plumb, near-vertical, short, NaN), cropStraightenFitted (0°, 90°, 45°, invalid sizes), the schema field, and an armed drag through TOOLS.crop setting the angle, fitting the frame, and disarming, plus a short line that only disarms, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: The held Ctrl/Cmd temporary Straighten and the angle readout beside the pointer are a later story; Classic Mode and Auto Center Preview stay out of scope.

userStories.title: Crop temporary Straighten and angle readout: holding Ctrl/Cmd with Crop draws a straighten line, and the line's angle shows beside the pointer
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's held-modifier Straighten and its Angle readout (crates/ui-egui/src/crop_straighten.rs set_held, mode, pointer with mods.command, draw, canvas::angle_readout) so I can level a horizon without reaching for the options-bar button and see the angle while I draw.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/crop-frame.js: pure cropAngleReadout(deg) ported from canvas::angle_readout: one decimal and a degree sign, never '-0.0°' and never '-180.0°' (-0.03 → '0.0°', -179.97 → '180.0°', 12.34 → '12.3°', -12.36 → '-12.4°').

TOOLS.crop.onDown starts a straighten line when state.cropStraighten is armed or Ctrl/Cmd is held (state.ctrlKey), and no crop drag is in progress; a Ctrl/Cmd-drag outside the frame draws the line instead of turning the frame. Release applies it exactly as the armed line (US-152); a held-modifier line does not touch the armed flag except to clear it as release does.

While a straighten line is drawn, drawCropTool draws a small 'Angle: <cropAngleReadout>' label beside the line's end, where the angle is the line's own angle atan2(-dy, dx) in degrees; nothing is drawn for a zero-length line.
TOOLS.crop.cursorAt returns 'crosshair' while Ctrl/Cmd is held with Crop active (passed in through state), so the turn cursor is not shown outside the frame.

tests/paint-crop-straighten-held.test.mjs covers cropAngleReadout's four cases, a Ctrl-drag outside the frame through TOOLS.crop setting the angle from (250, 60) to (0, 0) on a 200 x 100 canvas to atan(60/250), the same drag without Ctrl turning the frame instead, a Ctrl-down during an existing crop drag not starting a line, and the readout text recorded from a stub overlay's fillText, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: paint/pointer.js already sets state.ctrlKey to (ctrlKey || metaKey) on pointer down and move (false for a right button); use it rather than adding state.metaKey. Classic Mode and Auto Center Preview stay out of scope.

userStories.title: Crop frame readouts: W and H beside the pointer while drawing or resizing the frame, and the Angle while turning it
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Crop readouts (crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs frame_size, sizing, turning; canvas.rs marquee_readout, draw_value_readout) so I can see the frame's size and turn while I drag it.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/crop-frame.js: pure cropFrameSize(frame) ported from crop_ui.rs frame_size: [round(w), round(h)] each at least 1, or null when either is not finite.

While TOOLS.crop has a 'draw' drag whose pointer has moved off its anchor, or any resize drag, drawCropTool draws two readout rows 'W: <w> px' and 'H: <h> px' (cropFrameSize of state.cropFrame) beside the pointer; while a 'turn' drag is in progress it draws 'Angle: <cropAngleReadout(state.cropAngle)>' instead. A move ('inside') drag, an idle frame, and a draw drag that has not moved draw no readout. The pointer position rides on the drag record (the onMove x, y).

Readout text is drawn at a constant screen size (divide by zoom, as the Straighten readout does) and reuses the Straighten readout's stroke-then-fill style through one shared helper in paint/tools.js.

tests/paint-crop-readout.test.mjs covers cropFrameSize (rounding, the 1 px floor, NaN), a draw drag recording 'W: 120 px' / 'H: 40 px' from a stub overlay's fillText, an unmoved draw recording nothing, a resize recording the new size, a turn recording the Angle row, and a move recording nothing, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Paint has no Units & Rulers preference, so values are always px. Classic Mode's image turn (crop_mode::image_turn) is out of scope; the turn readout is the frame's own state.cropAngle. Show Transformation Values has no Paint preference; always show.

userStories.title: Crop Space reposition: holding Space while drawing a new crop frame moves it at its size instead of panning, and sizing resumes from the moved anchor
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Space-while-drawing reposition (crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs set_space, update CropDrag::Draw with space, space_repositions_the_frame_being_drawn) so I can place a frame I am drawing without starting over.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOLS.crop gains setSpace(ov, state, down) setting state.cropSpace; it is a no-op on the frame when no draw drag is in progress.

While a TOOLS.crop draw drag is in progress and state.cropSpace is true, onMove shifts the drag anchor (x0, y0) and the current corner by the pointer delta since the last move, so the frame keeps its size; when Space is released, the next move sizes the frame from the moved anchor. Move, resize, and turn drags ignore Space.
paint/paint.js: while the Crop tool has a draw drag in progress, Space keydown / keyup call TOOLS.crop.setSpace instead of starting the hand-pan; outside a crop draw Space pans as before.

tests/paint-crop-space.test.mjs ports space_repositions_the_frame_being_drawn on a 200 x 100 canvas: down (10, 10), move (50, 40), Space down, move (70, 50) gives [30, 20, 70, 50]; Space up, move and up at (90, 60) gives [30, 20, 90, 60]; plus a move drag with Space held moving normally, and a source check that paint.js routes Space to setSpace during a crop draw, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: paint.js already tracks state.spaceDown for the hand-pan (keydown / keyup on e.code Space); the crop draw must win over it only mid-draw. The drag record already carries the last pointer (drag.x, drag.y) from US-154.

userStories.title: Crop box Undo/Redo: while the Crop tool has frame history, Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z step the pending frame, not the document
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's crop box history (crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs CropStep, push_press_step, is_enabled, intercept, step; edit_undo_steps_the_crop_box_not_the_document, box_undo_and_redo_grey_out_when_their_stack_is_empty) so a frame I moved by mistake comes back without cancelling the crop.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/tools.js: TOOLS.crop keeps state.cropUndo and state.cropRedo arrays of steps { frame, angle, isDefault } (frame copied). A draw, move, resize, turn, or Straighten that changes the frame or angle pushes the step from its press onto cropUndo on release and clears cropRedo; a gesture that changes nothing pushes none. cancel and commit clear both stacks.

TOOLS.crop.stepHistory(ov, state, redo) pops one step from cropUndo (or cropRedo), pushes the current step onto the other stack, restores state.cropFrame, state.cropAngle, and state.cropDefault, redraws, and returns true; with nothing to pop it returns false and changes nothing. TOOLS.crop.historyEnabled(state, 'undo' | 'redo') returns null when both stacks are empty, else whether that stack has a step.

paint/paint.js: while the Crop tool is active and either stack has a step, Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z (and Ctrl+Y if paint.js already maps it) call TOOLS.crop.stepHistory instead of the document undo, and the Edit menu / undo buttons reflect historyEnabled (a stack with nothing left greys out instead of falling back to the document). With both stacks empty, undo is the document's as before.

tests/paint-crop-undo.test.mjs ports edit_undo_steps_the_crop_box_not_the_document on a 200 x 100 canvas: frame [40, 30, 100, 70] (not default), drag (70, 50) → (90, 50) gives x0 60; stepHistory(undo) restores [40, 30, 100, 70]; stepHistory(redo) gives x0 60 again; plus box_undo_and_redo_grey_out_when_their_stack_is_empty via historyEnabled, a no-change click pushing no step, cancel clearing both stacks, and a source check that paint.js routes Ctrl/Cmd+Z to TOOLS.crop.stepHistory, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: TOOLS.crop.onDown already records drag.prev, drag.deg, and drag.wasDefault, which are the press step. Straighten (TOOLS.crop.straighten) does not go through cropDrag, so capture its step there. The document undo in paint.js goes through undo() / redo(); find their keydown and menu entry points.

userStories.title: Perspective Crop tool: drag a box into a quad, drag its corners alone or move it, and Enter rectifies the quad onto an upright document
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Perspective Crop (crates/ui-egui/src/perspective_crop_ui.rs pointer, commit; crates/engine/src/perspective_crop_cmds.rs perspective_crop; crates/algo/src/transform.rs Homography, convex_quad; tests a_drag_without_area_leaves_no_quad, drag_a_box_move_a_corner_and_commit, perspective_crop_rectifies_a_skewed_ramp) so a photographed page or facade can be squared up.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/icons.js gains 'perspective-crop' copied from PhotoCraft assets/icons/perspective-crop.svg. paint/tools.js adds TOOLS.perspectiveCrop (label 'Perspective Crop', icon 'perspective-crop') listed after Crop in the toolbar; state.perspectiveQuad is [[x, y] x 4] in TL, TR, BR, BL order or null.

A drag with both width and height makes the box quad; a drag with no width or no height leaves no quad. A press within the handle reach of a corner moves that corner alone (keeping the press offset); a press inside the quad moves the whole quad. The overlay draws the quad, its corner handles, and a perspective grid, in red while convexQuad(quad) (a pure port of transform.rs convex_quad, wound like its box) is false.

paint/transform.js gains pure homographyFromQuad(quad, w, h) (the unit-square / rectangle to quad mapping of transform.rs Homography) and perspectiveCropImageData(src, quad, w, h) that samples through the existing bilinear sampler. Enter (or the options-bar commit) on a convex quad replaces every layer with the rectified w x h image in one 'Perspective Crop' undo step, w and h from the Crop W x H fields when set, else the quad's mean side lengths rounded; Escape (or cancel) drops the quad; a non-convex quad does not commit. Switching tools drops the quad. Add 'Perspective Crop' to COMMAND_ICONS only if historyIconName would not already resolve it from TOOLS.

tests/paint-perspective-crop.test.mjs ports a_drag_without_area_leaves_no_quad and drag_a_box_move_a_corner_and_commit on a 200 x 150 canvas (box (20, 10) to (120, 90) gives [[20,10],[120,10],[120,90],[20,90]]; corner drag (121, 89) to (141, 99) gives [140, 100]; mean side size 110 x 86), checks convexQuad on a bow-tie, and checks perspectiveCropImageData maps a skewed quad's corner pixels onto the output corners, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Four-click corner placement, Show Grid, and the W x H swap button are later stories. Reuse cropCanvas-style whole-stack undo (STACK_UNDO_LABELS in paint/stack-history.js) and keep historySource / layer masks in step as cropCanvas does.

userStories.title: Perspective Crop corner clicks: four clicks place the quad's corners in any order, ordered TL, TR, BR, BL
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Perspective Crop click placement (crates/ui-egui/src/perspective_crop_ui.rs pointer Up CLICK_PX, ordered, draw_overlay clicks; test drag_a_box_move_a_corner_and_commit's ordered assertion and a_drag_without_area_leaves_no_quad's click) so I can click a skewed page's corners directly instead of dragging a box and moving each corner.
acceptanceCriteria: With no quad, a press and release that moves no more than CROP_HANDLE_PX * 3 / 8 / zoom on each axis is a click: it appends its press point to state.perspectiveClicks; the fourth click makes state.perspectiveQuad = perspectiveOrdered(clicks) and clears the clicks. A drag with area clears the clicks and makes the box quad as before.

paint/tools.js exports pure perspectiveOrdered(points) (a port of perspective_crop_ui.rs ordered): sort by atan2 about the centroid (clockwise on screen), then rotate so the point with the least x + y comes first.

The overlay draws the clicked points as small white circles with an accent outline, joined by a line once there are two or more. TOOLS.perspectiveCrop.cancel, Escape, and switching tools clear the clicks; Enter and Escape are taken while clicks are pending even with no quad.

tests/paint-perspective-crop-clicks.test.mjs checks that a click on an empty tool records [[30, 30]] and no quad, that four clicks (10, 90), (100, 5), (0, 0), (90, 100) give [[0, 0], [100, 5], [90, 100], [10, 90]], and that a box drag after one click clears the clicks, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Show Grid and the W x H swap button stay later stories. Reuse drawPerspectiveCrop in paint/tools.js for the click markers.

userStories.title: Perspective Crop options bar: W x H swap, Front Image, Clear, and Show Grid
userStories.description: As an editor, I want the rest of PhotoCraft's Perspective Crop options bar (crates/ui-egui/src/perspective_crop_ui.rs options_bar, draw_overlay perspective_crop_grid, test the_options_bar_swap_button_swaps_w_and_h) so I can size the result from the document, swap or clear W and H, and hide the perspective grid.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.perspectiveCrop lists W, a swap iconAction titled "Swaps height and width", H, a Front Image action, a Clear action, a Show Grid checkbox (key pcropGrid, default true), then cancel and commit.
Swap exchanges state.toolOptions.crop cropW and cropH even though the Crop tool's Ratio is not W x H; Front Image sets them to the document width and height in px; Clear empties both.
drawPerspectiveCrop draws the grid lines only while pcropGrid is true; the outline and corner handles always draw.

tests/paint-perspective-crop-options.test.mjs checks the schema order, that swap turns cropW 4 / cropH 6 into 6 / 4 with the Crop ratio left unchanged, that Front Image on a 200 x 150 document gives "200" / "150", that Clear gives empty strings, and that turning Show Grid off draws fewer line segments on a stub overlay, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: The resolution field and unit are not in Paint's Crop W x H fields; leave them out. Reuse the Crop tool's _cropSwap patch shape and the _perspectiveCropAction intercept in paint.js.

userStories.title: Patch tool (Normal, Source / Destination): lasso the patch, drag it, and release heals the selection from the dragged-to place
userStories.description: As a retoucher, I want PhotoCraft's Patch Tool (crates/ui-egui/src/retouch_ui.rs patch_drags_selection, patch_offset, finish_patch, the Tool::Patch options bar; crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds/patch.rs Source / Destination) so I can repair an area with texture from somewhere else in the image.
acceptanceCriteria: TOOLS.patch exists right after healingBrush in TOOLS key order, label 'Patch', icon 'lasso-select' (copied into paint/icons.js from PhotoCraft assets/icons if missing).

A drag that starts inside the active selection without Shift or Alt drags the patch: the overlay shows the selection outline at the pointer offset; any other drag draws a freehand lasso selection with the same add / subtract / intersect modifier behavior as lasso (selectionMode(state)).
Exported pure patchOffset(start, end, bbox, W, H) rounds the drag delta to whole pixels and clamps it so the selection bbox stays on the W x H canvas (retouch_ui.rs patch_offset).

On release with a nonzero offset, pushUndo('Patch') runs, then Source mode heals the selected pixels with the pixels under the dragged outline and Destination mode heals the dragged-to area with the selected pixels, both through healStroke in paint/retouch.js with the selection mask as coverage. A zero offset changes no pixels and pushes no undo.
TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.patch has a Patch iconButtons row (key patchMode, Source default, Destination); Content-Aware is left out (out of the browser ceiling).

tests/paint-patch-tool.test.mjs checks the TOOLS order and icon, patchOffset rounding and clamping at each edge, that a Source patch of a 4x4 noisy square dragged onto a flat area makes the square flat-ish (max channel spread drops) while pixels outside the selection are unchanged, that Destination writes only inside the offset square, and that a zero-offset release leaves pixels unchanged, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Add patch to SELECTION_TOOLS in paint/pointer.js and the two tool-switch lists in paint/paint.js so its lasso selection is not committed away. Reuse healStroke (paint/retouch.js) and the lasso path / scanlineFill pattern; do not write another Poisson solve.

userStories.title: Patch drag live preview: while the patch is dragged, the canvas shows the area healed at the current offset, and release commits the exact result
userStories.description: As a retoucher, I want PhotoCraft's live Patch preview (crates/ui-egui/src/patch_preview.rs display_doc, retouch_cmds/patch.rs preview / heal_region_coarse) so I can see where the patch lands before I release it.
acceptanceCriteria: Exported pure healCoarse(w, h, ch, src, dst, mask, step) in paint/retouch.js ports heal_region_coarse: step 1 returns exactly seamlessClone's result; step > 1 solves the boundary mismatch on a ceil(w/step) x ceil(h/step) cell grid with membraneFill and bilinearly adds it to the full-resolution source inside the mask.

Exported pure patchPreview(src, W, H, mask, dx, dy, mode, maxCells = 128 * 128) in paint/retouch.js returns { box, data } for the healed area (box [x0, y0, x1, y1), data RGBA bytes of that box) using the smallest step whose grid fits maxCells, or null for a zero offset; it never writes src.

While the Patch tool drags the patch with a nonzero offset, onMove draws the preview box onto the overlay (putImageData at the box origin) under the moved selection outline; a zero offset shows only the outline. Release still commits through patchHeal with one 'Patch' undo, so the committed pixels do not depend on the preview.

tests/paint-patch-preview.test.mjs checks that healCoarse at step 1 equals seamlessClone, that a step-4 heal of a linear-ramp destination with a flat source stays within 0.02 of the ramp, that patchPreview with a large maxCells equals the committed patchHeal pixels inside its box for both Source and Destination, that a zero offset returns null, and that src is unchanged, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: patchTool and patchOffset live in paint/tools.js; state.patchDrag holds start, mask, bbox, edge (buildBoundaryPixels) and offset. Recompute the preview only when the offset changes. Reuse membraneFill / seamlessClone in paint/retouch.js; do not write another solver.

userStories.title: Ruler tool: drag a measuring line, drag its ends, and the options bar reads X, Y, W, H, A, L1 with Clear
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Ruler Tool (crates/ui-egui/src/analysis_ui.rs pointer / options_bar Tool::Ruler, crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs ruler_info) so I can measure distances and angles on the canvas without changing pixels.
acceptanceCriteria: Exported pure rulerInfo(ruler) in paint/tools.js ports ruler_info without a protractor: { x, y, w, h, angle, l1 } where (x, y) is the start, (w, h) = end − start, angle = atan2(−h, w) in degrees (counter-clockwise from +x, −180..180) and l1 the length, angle and l1 rounded to 4 decimals.

TOOLS.ruler (label 'Ruler', icon 'ruler' copied from PhotoCraft assets/icons into paint/icons.js, after eyedropper in TOOLS order) keeps state.ruler { start, end } (document px). A press within CROP_HANDLE_PX / zoom of the end or start drags that end; any other press starts a new ruler; Shift constrains the dragged end to 45° steps around the other end; a release of a new ruler shorter than 0.5 px clears it. The ruler pushes no undo and changes no pixels.
The overlay draws the ruler line with small end crosses while the Ruler tool is active; switching tools hides it and switching back shows it again.
TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.ruler shows read-only X, Y, W, H, A, L1 readouts of rulerInfo (blank with no ruler) and a Clear 'action' button disabled with no ruler that sets state.ruler = null.

tests/paint-ruler-tool.test.mjs checks rulerInfo values for a few lines (including angle sign with y down), new-ruler / end-drag / Shift-constrain / tiny-release-clears behavior on TOOLS.ruler with stub contexts, that no pixels or undo change, and the Clear action, with direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: The Alt-drag protractor, Straighten Layer, and Use Measurement Scale are later stories. Readouts can be TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA readout-style fields; renderToolOptions in paint/ui.js may need a small read-only type. Reuse CROP_HANDLE_PX from paint/crop-frame.js for the hit radius.

userStories.title: Ruler protractor: Alt-drag from an end starts a second arm, and the options bar reads the angle between the arms and L2
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Ruler protractor (crates/ui-egui/src/analysis_ui.rs pointer Tool::Ruler mods.alt, RulerHandle(2); crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs ruler_info Some(protractor)) so I can measure the angle between two lines that share a vertex.
acceptanceCriteria: rulerInfo(ruler) in paint/tools.js handles ruler.protractor [x, y]: angle is |atan2(−h, w) − atan2(−ey, ex)| in degrees folded to 0..180 (360 − a above 180), where (ex, ey) = protractor − start, and l2 is the protractor arm length, both rounded to 4 decimals; with no protractor l2 is null and the existing values are unchanged.

TOOLS.ruler: an Alt press within CROP_HANDLE_PX / zoom of the start or end (and a ruler present) starts the protractor arm at that vertex. A press near only the end swaps start and end first, so start is always the vertex. The arm end follows the pointer (Shift snaps to 45° around the vertex). A press near an existing protractor end drags it, checked before the end and start. A new ruler drops the protractor.
The overlay draws the protractor arm the same way as the main line (dark under white, end cross).
TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.ruler adds an L2 readout after L1 (blank with no protractor).

tests/paint-ruler-protractor.test.mjs checks rulerInfo with a protractor (a right angle, an obtuse angle above 180 folded back, L2), Alt-drag from the start and from the end (vertex swap), dragging the protractor end, Shift snapping, and that a new ruler clears the protractor, with stub contexts and direct assertions. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Builds on US-162 (state.ruler, rulerInfo, strokeRuler). pointer.js already sets state.altKey on down. Straighten Layer and Use Measurement Scale stay later stories.

userStories.title: Ruler Straighten Layer: the options bar's Straighten Layer turns the active layer so the ruler line lies on its nearest axis, then clears the ruler
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's Straighten Layer (crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs straighten_angle / straighten, the non-crop edit.transform path; crates/ui-egui/src/analysis_ui.rs options_bar Tool::Ruler secondary_button 'Straighten Layer') so I can level a tilted horizon by measuring it.
acceptanceCriteria: straightenAngle(ruler) is exported from paint/tools.js: a = atan2(−h, w) in degrees, result a − 90 · round(a / 90) (clockwise degrees onto the nearest axis). A line falling to the right (start [50, 50], end [150, 60]) gives −5.7106 to 4 decimals; [150, 40] gives +5.7106; a near-vertical [60, −50] gives −5.7106. The protractor is ignored.
TOOL_OPTION_SCHEMA.ruler gains a 'Straighten Layer' type 'action' field between L2 and Clear, disabledWhen ruler in [null, undefined], patching '_rulerAction': 'straighten'.

paint.js handles '_rulerAction' 'straighten': when |straightenAngle| < 1e-9 nothing happens; otherwise it pushes undo 'Straighten' first, rotates the active layer's pixels clockwise on screen by that angle about the canvas centre with the bilinear sampler in paint/transform.js (canvas size unchanged, uncovered pixels transparent), then sets state.ruler to null and refreshes the options bar. 'Straighten' has a COMMAND_ICONS entry in paint/history.js.

The pixel rotation is a pure exported function (for example straightenImageData(img, deg) in paint/transform.js) with direct assertions: a 90° turn of a small image maps known pixels, 0° is the identity, and a non-axis angle leaves the corners transparent.

tests/paint-ruler-straighten.test.mjs covers straightenAngle (the three PhotoCraft cases above, an exact horizontal line giving 0), the options-bar field order and disabledWhen, and the pure rotation, with direct assertions and no browser. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Builds on US-162 / US-163 (state.ruler, rulerInfo, the '_rulerAction' patch). PhotoCraft's crop path (rotate the canvas and crop to the inscribed rectangle on a background layer) is left for a later story; this one is the edit.transform layer path. Use Measurement Scale stays later.

userStories.title: Ruler Straighten on the background layer: turn the canvas by the ruler's angle and crop to the largest inscribed rectangle
userStories.description: As an editor, I want PhotoCraft's crop path of Straighten (crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs straighten with crop = true, inscribed) so that straightening a flattened photo levels it without transparent corners.
acceptanceCriteria: inscribedSize(w, h, rad) is exported from paint/transform.js as a port of PhotoCraft analysis_cmds inscribed: inscribedSize(200, 100, 10°) is [191.1229, 67.8425] to 4 decimals, inscribedSize(200, 100, 45°) is [70.7107, 70.7107], and inscribedSize(w, h, 0) is [w, h].

straightenCropRect(w0, h0, newW, newH, deg) is exported from paint/transform.js: cw = clamp(floor(inscribed w), 1, newW), ch likewise, x = round((newW − cw) / 2), y = round((newH − ch) / 2), returned as { x, y, width, height }.

paint.js straightenLayer: when the active layer is the bottom layer (state.layers[0], which rotateCanvas fills with the background color), it pushes one undo 'Straighten', turns the whole canvas clockwise by straightenAngle through the rotateCanvas pixel path, then crops through cropCanvas to straightenCropRect, so the result has no transparent or background-filled corners; on any other layer it keeps the US-164 same-size layer turn. Either way state.ruler ends null. One undo restores the original size and pixels.

tests/paint-ruler-straighten-crop.test.mjs covers inscribedSize (the three cases above, plus a tall image where w < h swaps the result), straightenCropRect (centred, clamped to the turned size, at least 1 x 1), and the composed pure pixels (rotateImageData then the crop rect) on a small opaque image leaving every output pixel opaque, with direct assertions and no browser. Run node --test on this story's test file only. Do not run anything else.
userStories.notes: Builds on US-164 (straightenAngle, straightenImageData, the '_rulerAction' 'straighten' handler). If rotateCanvas and cropCanvas each push undo, factor their bodies so the compound takes one 'Straighten' entry (STACK_UNDO_LABELS if the canvas size changes). Use Measurement Scale stays later.

userStories.description: As an editor, I want an eye on the RGB, Red, Green, and Blue rows of the Channels panel so I can hide a color channel or view one alone, as PhotoCraft does (channels_panel.rs eye_resp → channel.setVisible; channel_cmds.rs set_visible; channel_view.rs render_with_source). Paint's channel rows are text only and the view always shows the full composite.
acceptanceCriteria: paint/channels.js exports toggleColorVisible(hidden, name): hidden is [r, g, b] booleans (true = hidden), never mutated. 'Red' / 'Green' / 'Blue' flip that entry; 'RGB' shows all three if any is hidden, else hides all three (set_visible ChanRef::Composite). An unknown name returns the input array itself.

paint/channels.js exports channelViewPixels(img, hidden): returns null when no channel or every channel is hidden (the plain composite, render_with_source returns None). With exactly one channel visible, every pixel is that channel's byte as gray, alpha 255. With two visible, the hidden channel's byte is 0, alpha 255. The input img is not mutated; the result is { width, height, data: Uint8ClampedArray }.
